guide.summary: Jesus' birth fulfills centuries of prophetic promises. Mary is chosen as the mother of the Savior, announced by an angel, visited by shepherds and magi. Simeon and Anna recognize the arrival of the long-awaited Messiah. Jesus the child grew in wisdom and grace, as the true Son of God.

keyVerses.text: In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary.

The angel said to them, "Don't be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all people. For there is born to you, this day, in the city of David, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord."
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom, and God's grace was upon him.

guide.summary: Jesus' ministry begins with his baptism and the confirmation of the Father. He overcomes the temptations in the wilderness and calls his first disciples. His first miracle in Cana reveals his power. Nicodemus learns about being born again. Everything converges on the central truth: God loves the world and offers eternal life through the Son.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

guide.summary: Jesus teaches the way to the Kingdom through the Beatitudes and the Lord's Prayer, revealing that true life consists in trusting him. His parables challenge crowds to think about faith and priorities. His miracles demonstrate compassion and divine power: he feeds thousands, walks on water, heals the sick, and raises the dead.

guide.summary: The climax of Jesus' life: his triumphal entry into Jerusalem, Last Supper, unjust trial, and sacrificial death. The disciples abandon him at the cross. But on the third day he rises, defeating death and sin. He appears to the disciples, commissions them, and returns to the Father, leaving the Holy Spirit as comforter.
